Dr. Prabuchandran K.J. is with the Department of Computer Science and
arxiv-2310-05911.creator: Arghyadeep Barat, Prabuchandran.K.J, and Shalabh Bhatnagar
arxiv-2310-05911.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Arghyadeep Barat, Prabuchandran.K.J, and Shalabh Bhatnagar. In this paper, we consider the problem of finding an optimal energy management policy for a network of sensor nodes capable of harvesting their own energy and sharing it with other nodes in the network. We formulate this problem in the discounted cost Markov decision process framework and obtain good energy-sharing policies using the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm.

arxiv-2402-15134.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kun Yi, Qi Zhang, Hui He, Kaize Shi, Liang Hu, Ning An, Zhendong Niu. Multivariate time series (MTS) forecasting is crucial in many real-world applications. To achieve accurate MTS forecasting, it is essential to simultaneously consider both intra- and inter-series relationships among time series data. However, previous work has typically modeled intra- and inter-series relationships separately and has disregarded multi-order interactions present within and between time series data, which can seriously degrade forecasting accuracy.

arxiv-2508-11317.title: Logic Unseen: Revealing the Logical Blindspots of Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2508-11317.creator: Yuchen Zhou, Jiayu Tang, Shuo Yang, Xiaoyan Xiao, Yuqin Dai, Wenhao Yang
arxiv-2508-11317.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yuchen Zhou, Jiayu Tang, Shuo Yang, Xiaoyan Xiao, Yuqin Dai, Wenhao Yang. Vision-Language Models (VLMs), exemplified by CLIP, have emerged as foundational for multimodal intelligence. However, their capacity for logical understanding remains significantly underexplored, resulting in critical “logical blindspots” that limit their reliability in practical applications. To systematically diagnose this, we introduce LogicBench, a comprehensive benchmark with over 50,000 vision-language pairs across 9 logical categories and 4 diverse scenarios: images, videos, anomaly detection, and medical diagnostics.

pmc-11436174.title: On the Development of an Acoustic Image Dataset for Unexploded Ordnance Classification Using Front-Looking Sonar and Transfer Learning Methods
pmc-11436174.creator: Piotr Ściegienka, Marcin Blachnik, Jingjing Wang
pmc-11436174.description: This research aimed to develop a dataset of acoustic images recorded by a forward-looking sonar mounted on an underwater vehicle, enabling the classification of unexploded ordnances (UXOs) and objects other than unexploded ordnance (nonUXOs). The dataset was obtained using digital twin simulations performed in the Gazebo environment utilizing plugins developed within the DAVE project.

pmc-11641897.title: Genome-Wide Identification and Expression Analysis of Carotenoid Cleavage Dioxygenase Genes in Salvia miltiorrhiza
pmc-11641897.creator: Minyu Shou, Qinzhe Lin, Lulu Peng, Zijie Wang, Ying Xu, Jiaochen Qi, Degang Zhao, Min Shi, Guoyin Kai
pmc-11641897.description: In the process of catalyzing carotenoids into various apocarotenoids and other derivatives, carotenoid cleavage dioxygenases (CCDs) play key roles. However, little information on CCDs has been reported in regard to Salvia miltiorrhiza. In this study, a total of 21 CCD genes were identified in the whole genome of S. miltiorrhiza, mainly distributed between five chromosomes.

pmc-12413741.title: Sensitivity of Different Clinical Outcome Measures in Assessing Adults With Becker Muscular Dystrophy
pmc-12413741.creator: Esther J. Schrama, Zaïda Koeks, Nienke M. Van De Velde, Iris Alleman, Jules J. van Benthem, Pieteke W. van Weperen, Melissa T. Hooijmans, Hermien E. Kan, Pietro Spitali, Nina Ajmone Marsan, Douwe E. Atsma, Hermine A. van Duyvenvoorde, Jan J.G.M. Verschuuren, Erik H. Niks
pmc-12413741.description: Background and ObjectivesSlow and highly variable disease progression in Becker muscular dystrophy (BMD) stresses the need to develop sensitive outcome measures for clinical trials. We evaluated responsiveness of different outcome measures in adult patients with BMD over 3 years and explored if the sensitivity of outcome measures can be increased by selecting on phenotype or genotype.

pmc-12540535.title: Urban thermal data analysis over the period 1948–2022: a case study of Ljubljana, Slovenia
pmc-12540535.creator: Zalika Črepinšek, Zala Žnidaršič, Tjaša Pogačar
pmc-12540535.description: The aim of the study was to characterize the intensity, frequency and duration of extreme high temperature events and their variability over a period of 75 years (1948–2022) for Ljubljana, Slovenia. This study uses 23 thermal indices recommended by the WMO (ETCCDI) based on daily maximum and minimum air temperatures, retrieved from the Slovenian Environment Agency.
